In announcing these results, Chief Executive Officer Tim Laney shared, “This was a deeply disappointing quarter. We reported a net loss of $8.8 million, driven primarily by $40.6 million of provision expense tied to a handful of specifically identified commercial credits, mainly in the franchise and healthcare industries. We take these credit events seriously and have made a series of both personnel and process improvements in these specific coverage areas of our business. To that end, none of these actions were driven by our regulators, and we will be relentless in our focus to meet the highest standards of credit risk management.”


Mr. Laney added, “Our margin expansion and deposit growth are positive, and all integration activity has been a success. Our responsibility is to protect the bank while driving to our target of a dollar plus of earnings per share in the fourth quarter. While the third quarter represented a painful setback, I believe our team is more than capable of delivering for our clients, communities and shareholders.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Results**
***(All comparisons refer to the second quarter of 2026, except as noted)***


As previously announced, third quarter results were impacted by elevated provision expense related to specifically identified credits addressed during the quarter. During the third quarter of 2026, net loss totaled $8.8 million, or ($0.20) per diluted share, compared to net income of $26.5 million, or $0.58 per diluted share. The quarter’s results were impacted by $40.6 million of provision expense, $15.2 million of pre-tax acquisition and restructuring expense, and a $4.0 million impairment on a third-party FinTech partnership investment classified within other securities. Fully taxable equivalent pre-provision net revenue totaled $30.9 million, compared to $36.3 million. The return on average tangible assets totaled (0.23)%, compared to 0.96%, and the return on average tangible common equity totaled (2.32)%, compared to 9.70%. Adjusting for the $15.2 million of pre-tax acquisition and restructuring related expenses in the third quarter, adjusted net income totaled $2.9 million, or $0.06 per diluted share, and adjusted fully taxable equivalent pre-provision net revenue totaled $46.1 million. The adjusted return on average tangible assets totaled 0.16%, and the adjusted return on average tangible common equity totaled 1.62%.


**Net Interest Income**
Fully taxable equivalent net interest income increased $3.6 million to $115.2 million, primarily due to average interest earning assets growth of $69.9 million and one additional day during the third quarter. The fully taxable equivalent net interest margin expanded six basis points to 4.00%, driven by a nine basis point increase in earning asset yields. The cost of deposits increased one basis point to 1.94%.


**Loans**
Loans increased $119.4 million, or 4.9% annualized, to $9.9 billion at September 30, 2026. We generated quarterly loan fundings of $819.3 million, led by commercial loan fundings of $351.2 million.


**Asset Quality and Provision for Credit Losses**
The Company recorded provision expense of $40.6 million during the quarter, compared to $1.5 million. The increase was primarily driven by write downs on specifically identified commercial loans, principally within the franchise and healthcare industries, related to credit events impacting the third quarter. Annualized net charge-offs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled 0.85% of average total loans. Non-performing loans totaled 0.44% of total loans at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.31%, and non-performing assets totaled 0.50% of total loans and OREO at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.35%. The allowance for credit losses as a percentage of loans was 1.11% at September 30, 2026, compared to 1.13%.


**Deposits**
The Company maintains a low cost, diversified deposit franchise. Average total deposits increased $96.0 million to $10.3 billion, and average transaction deposits (defined as total deposits less time deposits) increased $102.9 million to $9.0 billion. The loan to deposit ratio totaled 93.8% at September 30, 2026, compared to 94.1%. The mix of transaction deposits to total deposits increased 20 basis points to 88.0% at September 30, 2026.


**Non-Interest Income**
Non-interest income totaled $13.5 million, compared to $19.8 million, during the second quarter. Other non-interest income decreased $5.9 million and included $4.0 million of impairment on a third-party FinTech partnership investment classified within other securities. Mortgage banking income decreased $0.6 million driven by the current rate environment. These decreases were partially offset by a $0.3 million increase in bank card fee income.


**Non-Interest Expense**
Non-interest expense totaled $97.8 million, compared to $95.0 million. Included in the third and second quarters were acquisition and restructuring related expenses of $15.2 million and $11.2 million, respectively. Excluding these items, third quarter adjusted non-interest expense decreased $1.1 million, to $82.6 million, compared to $83.7 million. The linked-quarter decrease reflects management’s continued execution on operational synergies following the successful third-quarter integration of Vista’s core systems. Third quarter’s expenses include one additional payroll day compared to the second quarter and $1.4 million of OREO and problem loan expenses. The fully taxable equivalent efficiency ratio totaled 76.0%, compared to 72.3%. The adjusted fully taxable equivalent efficiency ratio totaled 62.3%, compared to 61.8%.


Income tax benefit totaled $3.2 million, compared to income tax expense of $6.1 million in the previous quarter. The effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 17.3%, compared to 18.3% for the same period prior year.


**Capital**
Common book value per share totaled $36.71 at September 30, 2026, compared to $37.48 at June 30, 2026. Tangible book value per share totaled $25.37, compared to $26.23, primarily reflecting the quarterly dividend payment, share repurchases and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss due to changes in the interest rate environment.


NBHC executed $11.9 million of share buybacks in the third quarter as part of its ongoing capital strategy. Capital ratios continue to be well in excess of federal bank regulatory agency “well capitalized” thresholds. The tier 1 leverage ratio totaled 10.00%, and the common equity tier 1 capital ratio totaled 11.69% at September 30, 2026. Shareholders’ equity totaled $1.6 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.7 billion.


**Recent Events**
On October 24, 2026, NBH Bank (the “Bank”) entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Palm Beach, Florida banking center location, including the banking center’s loans and deposits. The sale is expected to result in a reduction of the Bank’s total assets of approximately $0.2 billion, including total loans of approximately $0.2 billion, and a reduction of total deposits of approximately $0.2 billion. The agreement provides for a deposit premium of 5.00%, subject to a minimum deposit premium of $8.8 million. The Bank expects to close the transaction in mid-2027.


**Year-Over-Year Review**
***(All comparisons refer to the first nine months of 2025, except as noted)***


Net income totaled $38.5 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, compared to $93.5 million or $2.43 per diluted share. Current year results were impacted by $46.1 million of provision expense, primarily due to third quarter credit events within the franchise and healthcare industries, $42.0 million of pre-tax acquisition and restructuring expense, and a $4.0 million impairment on a third-party FinTech partnership investment classified within other securities. Fully taxable equivalent pre-provision net revenue totaled $99.4 million, compared to $129.0 million. The return on average tangible assets totaled 0.50%, compared to 1.38%, and the return on average tangible common equity totaled 5.01%, compared to 13.05%. Adjusting for $42.0 million and $1.7 million of pre-tax acquisition and restructuring related charges for the nine months 2026 and 2025, respectively, adjusted net income totaled $70.9 million, or $1.56 per diluted share, compared to adjusted net income of $94.9 million, or $2.47 per diluted share. Adjusted, the fully taxable equivalent pre-provision net revenue increased $10.6 million, or 8.1%, to $141.4 million. The adjusted return on average tangible assets totaled 0.87%, and the adjusted return on average tangible common equity totaled 8.67%.


Fully taxable equivalent net interest income increased $69.6 million, or 26.0%, to $337.7 million. Average earning assets increased $2.2 billion, or 24.4%, driven by $500.9 million of average originated loan growth and loans acquired through the Vista acquisition. The Vista acquisition added $1.9 billion in total loans on January 7, 2026. The fully taxable equivalent net interest margin expanded five basis points to 4.00%, primarily driven by an eight basis point improvement in the cost of funds.


Loans outstanding increased $2.5 billion, or 33.2%, to $9.9 billion. New loan fundings over the trailing twelve months totaled a record $3.1 billion, led by commercial fundings of $1.7 billion.


The Company recorded $46.1 million of provision expense for credit losses, compared to $8.7 million. The increase was primarily driven by write downs on specifically identified commercial loans, primarily within the franchise and healthcare industries, related to credit events impacting the third quarter. Annualized net charge-offs totaled 0.85%, compared to 0.27%. Non-performing loans totaled 0.44% of total loans at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.36%, and non-performing assets totaled 0.50% of total loans and OREO at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.37%. The allowance for credit losses as a percentage of loans totaled 1.11% at September 30, 2026, compared to 1.19% at September 30, 2025.


Average deposits increased $2.0 billion to $10.2 billion, and average transaction deposits increased $1.8 billion to $8.9 billion compared to the same period prior year. The mix of transaction deposits to total deposits increased 167 basis points to 88.0% at September 30, 2026. The Vista acquisition added $2.2 billion of total deposits, including $2.0 billion of transaction deposits and $0.2 billion of time deposits on January 7, 2026.


Non-interest income totaled $51.3 million, compared to $53.1 million, decreasing due to $4.0 million of impairment on a third-party FinTech partnership investment within other securities and a $1.8 million decrease in mortgage banking income driven by the current rate environment. These decreases were mostly offset by increases in our diversified sources of fee income including service charges, bank card fees, trust income and swap fee income.


Non-interest expense totaled $289.6 million, compared to $192.2 million. Included in the periods were $42.0 million and $1.7 million of acquisition and restructuring expenses during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Excluding these items, the current period adjusted non-interest expense totaled $247.8 million, an increase from the same period prior year primarily due to our recent acquisition. Occupancy and equipment expense during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, included a full period of 2UniFiSM capitalized asset depreciation in connection with the launch of 2UniFi in the third quarter of 2025. The fully taxable equivalent efficiency ratio totaled 74.5%, compared to 59.8% in the same period prior year. The adjusted fully taxable equivalent efficiency ratio totaled 61.8% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 57.5%.


Income tax expense decreased $13.0 million to $8.0 million driven by lower pre-tax income in the current period. The effective tax rate was 17.3%, compared to 18.3% in the prior year.

**About National Bank Holdings Corporation**
National Bank Holdings Corporation is a bank holding company created to build a leading community bank franchise, delivering high quality client service and committed to stakeholder results. Through its bank subsidiaries, NBH Bank and 2UniFi Bank, National Bank Holdings Corporation operates a network of over 90 banking centers, serving individual consumers, small, medium and large businesses, and government and non-profit entities. Its banking centers are located in its core footprint of Colorado, the greater Kansas City region, Texas, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico, Idaho, and Palm Beach, Florida. Its comprehensive residential mortgage banking group primarily serves the bank’s core footprint. Its trust and wealth management business is operated through its trust and wealth department under Bank of Jackson Hole Trust & Wealth, a division of NBH Bank. NBH Bank operates its core banking business under a single state charter through the following brand names as divisions of NBH Bank: in Colorado, Community Banks of Colorado and Community Banks Mortgage; in Kansas and Missouri, Bank Midwest and Bank Midwest Mortgage; in Texas, Utah, New Mexico, Idaho, in Palm Beach, Florida, Vista Bank; and in Wyoming, Bank of Jackson Hole, Bank of Jackson Hole Mortgage and Bank of Jackson Hole Trust & Wealth. Additional information about National Bank Holdings Corporation can be found at[www.nationalbankholdings.com](http://www.nationalbankholdings.com/) .


For more information visit:[cobnks.com](http://cobnks.com/) ,[bankmw.com](http://bankmw.com/) ,[bankofjacksonhole.com](http://bankofjacksonhole.com/) ,[vistabank.com](http://vistabank.com/) , or[nbhbank.com](http://nbhbank.com/) , or connect with any of our brands on LinkedIn.


**About Non-GAAP Financial Measures**
Certain financial measures and ratios we present are supplemental measures that are not required by, or are not presented in accordance with, U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). We refer to these financial measures and ratios as “non-GAAP financial measures.” We consider the use of select non-GAAP financial measures and ratios to be useful for financial and operational decision making and useful in evaluating period-to-period comparisons. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance by excluding certain expenditures or assets that we believe are not indicative of our primary business operating results. We believe that management and investors benefit from referring to these non-GAAP financial measures in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, analyzing and comparing past, present and future periods.


These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with GAAP and you should not rely on non-GAAP financial measures alone as measures of our performance. The non-GAAP financial measures we present may differ from non-GAAP financial measures used by our peers or other companies. We compensate for these differences by providing the equivalent GAAP measures whenever we present the non-GAAP financial measures and by including a reconciliation of the impact of the components adjusted for in the non-GAAP financial measure so that both measures and the individual components may be considered when analyzing our performance. A reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to the comparable GAAP financial measures is included at the end of the financial statement tables.
